claims.text: Reducing laser power during L-PBF corresponds to lowering volumetric energy density.
Lower laser energy during L-PBF of AlCrFeNiSi will improve mechanical integrity.
Lower laser power reduces peak temperatures during solidification.
Lower laser power reduces steep thermal gradients during solidification.
Reduced peak temperatures and thermal gradients decrease the driving force for elemental segregation.
Lower laser energy reduces residual thermal-stress buildup in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Lower laser power reduces defect formation in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing residual thermal stress will reduce hot cracking.
Low-energy L-PBF will produce a more refined and uniform AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Low-energy L-PBF will diminish segregation of low-melting components at grain boundaries.
Low-energy L-PBF will reduce dendritic and intergranular defects.
Lower-energy AlCrFeNiSi parts will have higher density than higher-power conventionally processed samples, approaching or exceeding 99%.
Lower-energy AlCrFeNiSi parts will exhibit fewer microstructural defects and lower residual stresses than the higher-power baseline.
Lower-energy AlCrFeNiSi parts will have higher ductility and strength than the higher-power baseline.
Analogous HEA samples processed at higher laser power exhibit greater segregation, higher residual-stress concentrations, and more hot cracking.
The intervention is effective only within a low-energy processing window that still provides sufficient melting and avoids incomplete fusion.
The proposed validity is limited to additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi and is not asserted to transfer directly to bulk or other processing routes.
In CoCrFeNiCu, low laser power is reported to minimize defects and improve microstructure and mechanical performance.
